scope: All five owned sources read. Exact transport framing/configuration/deadline and cooperative owned process-group cleanup reviewed. Actual native SQLite worker and JSON/domain codec are separate.

checks.framing: Unsigned32 big-endian nonempty body<=1048572; exact response length; no trailing bytes; aggregate output<=1048576; UTF8 and exit0 required.
checks.deadline: Monotonic5000ms begins before config hashing; remaining budget given guardian; success later than original deadline refused. Cleanup has separate500ms bound and outer5700ms watch returns CleanupUnknown.
checks.cleanup: Leader retained unreaped while group receives SIGKILL; /proc zombie observation handles descendants retaining stdout; direct child reaped. Parent monitor closes owned port on caller death. Exceptions return finite uncertain/cleanup-unknown codes.
checks.configuration: Absolute local paths without dot/dotdot/NUL, executable regular single-link size<=16MiB, SHA256 verified each invocation. Trusted local configuration is not IAM or runtime authority.
checks.isolation: MAX65536 and ETS8192 source dependencies independently hashed unchanged; storage facade separate.

limitations: Tests use compiled EOF-sensitive fixture, not native SQLite; no canonical DB writes or Telegram traffic occurred.
Success body remains untrusted domain input until strict codec validation. No automatic retry.
Uncertain does not certify that no operation committed or that cleanup completed. Native worker must be observed quiescent before receipt lookup/reconciliation; CleanupUnknown remains a hold.
Only direct child is reaped; descendants deliberately creating sessions require service cgroup. No hostile same-UID filesystem/path isolation claim.

No physical quota, power-loss durability, actual native-worker compatibility, service release or global admission proved.
